title: Tiffin manifest v1
description: The project manifest: the evaluated form of tiffin.config.ts. Everything except `project` is optional; omitted fields get the defaults described on each property.

version.description: Version of the manifest format. Always 1. Default 1.

project.description: Project slug: a lowercase letter followed by up to 39 lowercase letters, digits or single dashes, not ending in a dash (1-40 chars).

resources.description: How much of the box the project's apps (production and previews) may use. Absent means automatic: the project grows into whatever the box has free, shares the CPU fairly with other projects under contention, and can never take the memory the platform or other projects' running apps need (a box-wide default share, if the owner set one, still applies). Set any field to give the project a fixed budget; when memoryMB and maxSharePercent are both set, the lower limit wins. Changes apply live, without restarting apps.

sleepAfter.description: Lets the project's production apps sleep when nobody uses them: after this long with no requests and no job, cron or workflow deliveries, their containers stop (freeing memory and CPU; images, data, routes and env stay) and the next request or delivery starts them again, which takes a few seconds. Hours or days, 1h to 30d, such as "24h", "7d" or "14d". Absent: they never sleep. Previews sleep after 15 idle minutes whatever this says.

apps.description: Apps keyed by name. App names follow the same slug rules as `project`. An app is one deployable unit.

services.description: Box-provided backends the project uses. A service that is absent is not provisioned. The dashboard calls them Database (postgres), Cache (valkey), Files (storage), Auth, Email and Analytics; `database`, `cache` and `files` are accepted here too and stored under the canonical name. Jobs are the top-level `queues` and `crons`, not a service.

crons.description: Scheduled calls, keyed by name. Cron names follow the same slug rules as `project`. Each cron sends an HTTP request on the schedule to its app's path (pushed internally, so worker apps, which have no routes, are valid targets) or to a `url` outside the box.

queues.description: Named job queues, keyed by name. Queue names follow the same slug rules as `project`. The box pushes each job sent to a queue to its app's path as a signed HTTP request (worker apps, which have no routes, are valid targets) and retries failures with backoff. A queue you do not declare still works with defaults once an app sends to it; declaring it sets its target, limits and retry policy.

topics.description: Topics fan messages out to subscribed queues, keyed by name: a lowercase letter followed by up to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots or dashes, e.g. "order.created". A topic name must not also be a queue name.

domains.description: Options for the project's own domain names (not under the box domain), keyed by host name, e.g. "example.com". Which app serves a name is set by that app's `routes` ("example.com", "example.com/api"); a domain needs an entry here only for its options. The box checks every such name's DNS and gets its certificate once it points at the box: see GET /v1/projects/{project}/domains for the records to add and the live status.

env.description: Plain, non-secret environment variables shared by all apps. Secrets never live in the manifest; set them with `tiffin secrets`.

slug.description: Lowercase letter followed by up to 39 lowercase letters, digits or single dashes, not ending in a dash. Names join with "__" in database, role and key names, so a double dash would collide with another project's.

topicName.description: Lowercase letter followed by up to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots or dashes, e.g. "order.created".

propertyNames.description: Environment variable names are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE: letters A-Z, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

additionalProperties.description: Environment variable value. Must be a string.

app.description: One deployable unit: a web app or a worker.

path.description: Path to the app's source, relative to the manifest. Default ".".

framework.description: How the app is built and run. "next" = Next.js, "hono" = Hono on Bun, "bun" = any Bun server listening on $PORT, "static" = static files served directly by the proxy. Default "bun".

role.description: What an instance does. "web" serves HTTP on its routes; "worker" only receives queue and workflow pushes and must not have routes. Default "web".

routes.description: Hostnames (optionally with a path prefix) this app serves, e.g. "shop" (expands to shop.<box domain>), "example.com", "example.com/api". Default: the project name for its main app ("shop") and "<project>-<app>" for the others ("shop-docs"); the main app is the only web app, else the one named like the project, else "web", else the first by name. Workers must not have routes. Routes must be unique across all apps.

items.description: A hostname with an optional path prefix, e.g. "shop", "example.com" or "example.com/api".

instances.description: Number of instances to run, 1-16. Default 1.

memoryMB.description: Optional memory cap per instance (copy) in MiB, 64-8192. Default: no per-copy cap; the app's copies share their project's memory (see the project-level `resources`).

healthcheck.description: HTTP path polled to decide whether an instance is healthy. Default "/". Ignored for workers and static apps.

command.description: Starts the app instead of the start command the build detects (package.json `start`), e.g. "bun run worker.ts", so one source folder can run a web app and a worker. Applies from the next deploy. Not for static apps.

release.description: Runs once per deploy, after the build and before the new version takes traffic, in a one-off container of the new image with the app's env, e.g. "bunx drizzle-kit migrate". A failure stops the deploy and the running version keeps serving. Rollbacks do not run it, so migrations must work with the previous version too. Previews run it only against their own database branch. Not for static apps.

packages.description: Debian (apt) packages installed in the app's image, e.g. ["ffmpeg"] or ["chromium"], for apps that run programs beside their own code. Applies from the next deploy. Not for static apps.

disk.description: Folders, relative to the app's working directory (e.g. "data", "uploads/tmp"), that persist across deploys and restarts, each with a size: a list (["data"]) makes each 1GB, an object sets them ({"data": "5GB", "renders": "20GB"}). Writes past a folder's size fail with "disk full" (ENOSPC). Growing a folder applies at once, without a restart; shrinking one below what it holds is refused. Every production instance shares them; each preview gets its own, of the same size. A folder starts with what the image has at that path. Their sizes together must fit in the project's storage limit. Not for static apps.

items.description: A folder inside the app's working directory, e.g. "data".

timeoutSeconds.description: The most one request to the app may take, in seconds, 1-86400 (24 hours). Default 900 (15 minutes). Past it the box answers 504 Gateway Timeout, or cuts a response it is streaming. Not for static apps.

env.description: App-specific plain environment variables, merged over the top-level `env`.

git.description: Connects the app to a GitHub repository through the box's GitHub App (Settings › Git): every push to `branch` deploys to production, and pull requests get preview deploys. Absent: the app deploys only when asked.

assets.description: The build's client-asset directory (its JS, CSS and other files for browsers). The box copies it out of each build and serves its files itself, and keeps serving the previous release's files for a day, so pages loaded before a deploy keep working. Absent: the box finds it for Next.js, Nuxt, TanStack Start, SolidStart, React Router, Remix, SvelteKit (adapter-node) and Astro (@astrojs/node); for other apps it stays off.

dir.description: The directory in the build, relative to the app, e.g. "dist/client".

path.description: The URL path its files are served at, e.g. "/static". Default "/".

git.description: Where an app's code lives on GitHub.

repo.description: The repository, "owner/name", e.g. "acme/shop". The box's GitHub App must be installed on it.

branch.description: The production branch: every push to it deploys the app. Default "main".

path.description: The app's folder inside the repository, for monorepos, e.g. "apps/web". Default: the top of the repository.

previews.description: Which pull requests get a preview deploy at its own address. "same-repo": pull requests from branches of this repository. "forks": also pull requests from forks, whose code then runs on your box with the project's env and secrets. "off": no previews. Default "same-repo".

cron.description: One scheduled call into an app, or to an address outside the box (`url`). Set `app` or `url`.

schedule.description: A 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, fields separated by single spaces, e.g. "0 3 * * *") or one of @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly.

app.description: Name of the app to call. Must be an app defined in `apps`. Set `app` or `url`, not both.

url.description: An http(s) address outside the box to POST to instead of an app, e.g. "https://hooks.example.com/digest". Calls are signed (Tiffin-Signature, HMAC-SHA256 with the project's signing secret) and retried with backoff. Addresses of the box itself and private, loopback or link-local ones are refused.

path.description: Request path on the app. Must start with "/". Default "/cron/<cron name>". App targets only.

timezone.description: IANA time zone the schedule is read in, e.g. "America/New_York" or "Europe/London". Default UTC. When clocks change, a time that happens twice runs once and a time that is skipped runs at the change.

overlap.description: Run a tick even while the previous one is still queued or running. Default false: such a tick is skipped, and `queue crons list` shows when the last one was.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one call may take before it counts as failed and is retried, 5-3600 seconds. Default 60 (an app may extend it with heartbeats).

queue.description: One named job queue. Jobs sent to it are POSTed to `path` on `app`, or to `url` outside the box. Set `app` or `url`.

app.description: Name of the app that receives the jobs. Must be an app defined in `apps`. Set `app` or `url`, not both.

url.description: An http(s) address outside the box that jobs are POSTed to instead of an app, e.g. "https://hooks.example.com/orders". Each call is signed (Tiffin-Signature, HMAC-SHA256 with the project's signing secret). Addresses of the box itself and private, loopback or link-local ones are refused.

path.description: Request path jobs are POSTed to. Must start with "/". Default "/queues/<queue name>". App targets only.

concurrency.description: Most jobs of this queue running at once, 0-1000. Default 0: no limit.

keyConcurrency.description: Most jobs running at once for the same job key (the `key` option of a send), 0-1000. Default 0: no limit.

rateLimit.description: Most jobs started per `ratePeriodSeconds` for the same job key, 0-10000. Default 0: no limit.

ratePeriodSeconds.description: Window `rateLimit` counts in, in seconds, 1-86400. Default 60 when `rateLimit` is set; 0 when it is not.

maxAttempts.description: How many times a job is tried before it goes to the dead-letter queue, 1-100. Default 10.

leaseSeconds.description: How long one attempt may run without a response or heartbeat before it counts as failed, 5-3600. Default 60. Long jobs extend their lease with heartbeats. For a `url` target it is each call's timeout.

topic.description: A fan-out name: every message sent to the topic becomes one job for each subscriber queue, delivered and retried independently.

subscribers.description: Names of queues in this manifest. Each message sent to the topic is POSTed to every subscriber queue's app and path. Sorted and de-duplicated on normalization. Default: none (messages sent to the topic are dropped).

domainName.description: A full host name with at least one dot, lowercase, e.g. "example.com" or "shop.example.com".

domain.description: Options for one of the project's own domains.

www.description: "redirect" also serves www.<domain> and sends its visitors to <domain> (308, path and query kept); point www.<domain> at the box too. Default "" (off; to serve www.<domain> itself, add it to an app's routes).

resources.description: A project's share of the box. Every field is optional.

memoryMB.description: The most memory all of the project's app copies may use together, in MiB, at least 128. A hard cap and a guarantee: the memoryMB budgets of all projects together must fit in the memory the box keeps for apps (its memory minus what the platform needs), which the plan checks.

cpus.description: The most CPU time the project's apps may use together, in cores, in steps of 0.25 (e.g. 0.5, 1, 1.5). At most the box's CPU count, which the plan checks.

maxSharePercent.description: Caps the project at this percentage of the box, 5-100: of the memory the box keeps for apps and of its CPUs. A ceiling, not a reservation (shares of several projects may add up past 100), and it follows the box when it is resized.

postgres.description: Database: gives the project its own Postgres database. Provides DATABASE_URL to every app.

extensions.description: Postgres extensions to enable, e.g. "vector", "pg_cron". Sorted and de-duplicated on normalization.

statementTimeoutSeconds.description: Stops any one query of the project's after this many seconds, 1-3600. Default 30. A query can raise it for itself with SET LOCAL statement_timeout.

previews.description: Which database app previews use. "branch" (default): each preview gets its own copy-on-write copy of the database, made on its first deploy and deleted with the preview. "shared": previews use the production database and skip apps' release commands.

valkey.description: Cache: gives the project a Valkey (Redis-compatible) key-value/cache namespace. Provides REDIS_URL to every app.

maxMemoryMB.description: This project's cache limit in MiB, 1-65536. Default 64. Enforced while the project has a limit (resources, or the box's default share): keys with an expiry are cleared first, then writes are refused until it is under the limit.

storage.description: Files: gives the project S3-compatible object storage buckets. Provides S3_* (and AWS_*) env vars to every app.

buckets.description: Buckets keyed by name. Bucket names follow the same slug rules as `project`.

public.description: Public buckets are readable without a signature. Default false.

cors.description: Browser origins allowed to call the bucket's S3 API (presigned uploads and downloads): "https://example.com", a wildcard such as "https://*.example.com", or "*". Default: the project's own app hosts (previews and custom domains included) and http://localhost.

maxFileSize.description: Largest object an upload may create, in bytes. Default: no limit beyond the project's storage limit.

allowedTypes.description: MIME types uploads may have, e.g. ["image/*", "application/pdf"]. Default: any.

auth.description: Auth: gives the project user accounts and sessions. Needs postgres (users live there); add email too, for verification and sign-in mail. The box serves the auth endpoint at "/api/auth" on each app's own routes and exposes its base URL to every app as TIFFIN_AUTH_URL.

methods.description: Methods users can sign in with: "email" (email + password), "magic-link", "otp" (one-time code), "passkey", "google" or "github". Sorted and de-duplicated on normalization. Default ["email", "magic-link"].

organizations.description: Enables teams (organizations) with the roles owner, admin, member and viewer. Default true.

emailVerification.description: Whether new users must confirm their email address before they can sign in. Leave it out for automatic: required once the box has an SMTP relay (real mail goes out), not required while mail only reaches the dev inbox, so test sign-ups work at once. true or false forces it.

email.description: Lets the project send transactional email. Until an SMTP relay is configured on the box, mail goes to the box's dev inbox instead of the recipient.

from.description: Sender address, e.g. "hello@example.com". Must be a bare email address. Default "<project>@<box domain>", resolved by the box: leave it out to take the default.

analytics.description: Gives the project cookieless, first-party web analytics.

retentionDays.description: How long raw events are kept, in days, 1-3650. Default 365.
